knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement gives one continuous explanatory example, one categorical factor example, and states what an interaction term allows?
knowledge_checks.body: Select continuous, factor, and interaction warrant.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Age is continuous; region is a factor with levels. Interaction allows joint level-dependent effects beyond additive mains.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Continuous: age. Factor: region. Interaction: effect depends on level beyond mains.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating interaction as another main effect or omitting factor level coding.

choices.label: Continuous example: policyholder age. Categorical factor example: region with levels North/South. An interaction term allows the effect of one variable (for example age) to depend on the level of another (for example region), beyond main effects alone.
Continuous example: region North/South. Categorical factor example: age in years. An interaction is always unnecessary because main effects fully encode categories.
Continuous and factor variables are the same object in GLMs; an interaction term is just another main-effect slope on a continuous covariate.
Factors apply only outside GLMs; GLM linear predictors use only continuous covariates with no level coding.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Rating: continuous age x and factor region (levels North/South). Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Write eta with factor and interaction; refuse no-factor eta.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Factor indicator plus age-by-region interaction encodes level effects and slope change. Constant shift alone is not a full interaction story.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: η = β₀ + β₁ x + β₂ I_South + β₃ x I_South. Refuse no-factor eta and interaction-as-main.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting η = β₀ + β₁ x only or treating interaction as another main effect.

choices.label: η = β₀ + β₁ x + β₂ I_South + β₃ x times I_South with North baseline. Factors encode categorical levels; an interaction changes the age slope by region. It is not merely another additive main effect.
η = β₀ + β₁ x finishes explaining factors and interactions because region is known to the modeller.
η = β₀ + β₁ x + β₂ I_South only; the interaction is unnecessary because South adds a constant shift equal to an interaction.
Region enters as numeric 1 for North and 2 for South on the same slope as age; that is the GLM factor definition.

worked_example.title: Factor and interaction linear predictor for flood frequency
worked_example.problem_statement: A Poisson log-link flood-frequency GLM uses two binary factors: Coastal (1 if coastal postcode, else 0) and HighRise (1 if high-rise property, else 0), plus their interaction. The fitted linear predictor is η = −1.5 + 0.4 Coastal + 0.25 HighRise + 0.15 Coastal×HighRise. Compute η and μ = e^η for (a) coastal high-rise and (b) inland low-rise. State when the interaction term contributes.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Plug indicator patterns into η before exponentiating; check when C×H is nonzero.

steps.label: Coastal and high-rise
steps.attempt_cue: Set C = 1, H = 1 and evaluate η, then μ.
steps.explanation: All main effects and the interaction are active when both indicators equal 1.

steps.label: Inland and low-rise
steps.explanation: Only the intercept remains when both factors are at baseline.

steps.label: When the interaction applies
steps.attempt_cue: State the indicator condition for the 0.15 term.
steps.explanation: An interaction of two binary factors contributes only when both factors equal 1.
steps.calculation: 0.15 applies only if Coastal = 1 and HighRise = 1
steps.result: Interaction active only for coastal high-rise

worked_example.final_answer: Coastal & high-rise: η = −0.7, μ ≈ 0.4966. Inland & low-rise: η = −1.5. The interaction term 0.15 applies only when both factors equal 1.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Adding the interaction coefficient whenever either factor is present, or forgetting to include main effects when both indicators are 1.
